elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: Added: "The Company may assign this Agreement, without HDI's consent, to an affiliate..." — Company is a Customer alias, HDI the Vendor.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: "...or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of its assets" without HDI's consent — all three trigger events expressly listed.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: "HDI may not assign this Agreement without the Company's consent..." — direction runs against the Vendor only.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: "...consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld" attaches directly to the HDI assignment consent gate.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: "...and may in no event assign this Agreement to a competitor of the Company" — absolute bar, no consent override.

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: "...no change of control of the Company shall give HDI any right to terminate this Agreement"; no competing change-of-control termination right exists elsewhere (Section 4.1 is a mutual 90-day notice right).

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: Only the Company is given an affirmative successor assignment right; HDI's assignments, including to a successor, are gated on Company consent, so there is no mutual successor right.

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: No notice obligation appears in the retained or added language; neither party must notify the other of a successor assignment.
Consent is required only for HDI assignments; Company assignments outside the affiliate/successor carve-out are not subjected to any consent requirement in the operative text.

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The reasonableness standard is expressed only for Company consent to HDI assignments; there is no bilateral 'other assignments' consent mechanic to which it attaches.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all six preferred elements appear in operative language with correct party direction (Company assigns freely to affiliate/successor; HDI gated by consent not unreasonably withheld and absolutely barred from competitor assignment; change of control of Company yields HDI no termination right).

The fallback checklist is not independently satisfied (no written-notice mechanic, no mutual successor right, no consent gate on Customer's other assignments), but that does not matter because the preferred level is complete.

Minimal: the existing successors-and-assigns binding sentence is retained unchanged and only two sentences are inserted to close the gap; no survival tail, no added damages or procedural boilerplate, no requirement outside the preferred checklist.

Preserves intent: the retained 'no other person shall acquire or have any rights' language is consistent with permitted assignments to affiliates/successors and assigns; no undefined terms or dangling cross-references are introduced, and the Section 4.1 mutual 90-day termination right is untouched.
Severity remains high; the deviation classification is sound because the original clause imposed no restraint on Vendor assignment, including to a competitor, failing the fallback on material terms.
